Method of Attack: The attacker needs access to the process dump, swap file (pagefile.sys), hibernation file (hiberfil.sys), or a RAM dump of the complete system to exploit the bug using the PoC tool. The attack works regardless of whether the memory comes from a process dump, RAM dump, hibernation file, or swap file. The exploitable weakness results from the memory construction of residual strings for each character entered. When the word “Password” is typed, for example, residual strings such as •a, ••s, ••s, •••w, ••••o, •••••r, and •••••d are created. Except for the first character, the PoC program searches the dump for these patterns and offers possible password characters for each spot.
Impacted Systems: Potential consequences for Linux and macOS
Attack Vector: SecureTextBoxEx, KeePass’ customized text box used for entering the master password and additional passwords during editing, which keeps a record of the characters typed in memory.
